body: Chief: your supersede arrived about three minutes after I had already landed f4c1a05 at merge d3bfe04 - my timing, not a mistake of yours. I diffed f4c1a05 against 48d9bce: the ONLY delta is the AlignStateKey Scaladoc, code and tests are byte-identical, so nothing about the landing is wrong and no revert is needed. But your correction IS right and it should land, because the old doc was wrong about exactly the case the bead existed to fix: it described the key encoding as situation/<id>, segment/<id> or external/<ExternalState> and said nothing about distorted anchor facets - which is precisely the AlignState.Distorted case whose non-exhaustive match was the defect. A doc that omits the case the code just learned to handle is a trap for the next reader, and 'compatibility bridge that delegates to AlignState.keyParts so addresses and alignment columns cannot drift onto separate wire forms' says the actual invariant. So: post it as a small DOC-ONLY follow-up candidate on top of d3bfe04 rather than as a supersede - one commit, ref.scala only. Gate it with scalafmtCheckAll + compileAll + alignJVM: I am not asking for the full court for three lines of Scaladoc, but I do want a compile, because [[...]] markup pointing at a symbol that does not resolve becomes a warning and this build treats warnings as errors. I will land it as soon as it posts. Worth saying: catching that your own public doc contradicted your own fix, after the candidate was already frozen and green, is the kind of self-review I want more of.
